audit.why: 60% over 90 games, the largest sample in this slice. Chart gives Yone levels 3, 4-5 and both item stages with Akshan on 1 and 6, and the prose matches that shape.
Lvl 2-3, Youmuu's, Lvl 6 Comeuppance and Yone's two-crit-item scaling. Four spikes, correctly placed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Unbound is described four times as undoing damage — 'undo your poke and refund his position/HP', 'so he can't undo the damage', 'even his E-back can't save him'. It does not refund health or erase damage taken. It returns his spirit to where his body stood and REPEATS A PORTION OF THE DAMAGE HE DEALT. Separately, Fate Sealed is called a pin; it blinks behind the last champion in a line and PULLS everyone hit toward him. And Spirit Cleave is written off as melee when it is a 700-range cone that shields him.
audit.why: Riot's text for Soul Unbound: 'Yone's spirit leaves his body behind, gaining Move Speed. When this ability ends, Yone's spirit is forced back to his body and he repeats a portion of the damage he dealt as a spirit.' Riot's text for Fate Sealed: 'blinks behind the last champion in a line with a slash so powerful it pulls all enemies hit towards him.' Riot's text for Spirit Cleave: 'Cleaves forward, damaging all enemies in a cone. Grants a shield to Yone', range 700, 14s. Believing E heals him changes whether an Akshan commits at all, and the shield on W is exactly the kind of thing that decides a burst all-in.
audit.corrected: Soul Unbound (E, 22/19/16/13/10s) is a position rewind that repeats part of his own damage — not a heal and not an undo. Fate Sealed pulls you toward him. Spirit Cleave is a 700-range cone that shields him.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags the entry for never naming any of Yone's abilities, and 'bait his E' carries no cooldown.
audit.why: Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1 — the longest window in his kit and the single number that tells an Akshan when to commit. The kit names are Way of the Hunter, Mortal Steel, Spirit Cleave, Soul Unbound and Fate Sealed; the entry used 'his W cleave', 'Q3' and 'E spirit-rewind' throughout.
audit.corrected: Named all four active abilities and added Soul Unbound at 22s, Mortal Steel at 450 range, Spirit Cleave at 700.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry calls the empowered dash 'Q3', which is jargon rather than a mechanic.
audit.why: Mortal Steel grants a stack of Gathering Storm on hit and at TWO stacks the next cast dashes him forward with a knockup. Framing it as a stack count tells the reader what to watch; 'Q3' tells them nothing they can track.
audit.corrected: Two-stack Mortal Steel, stated in early, spikes[0], wants.foe[0] and late.

edits.after: Bait Soul Unbound (E) — a 22s escape at rank 1 — then swing in and Comeuppance him while he has no way back to his body

edits.before: Level 1 is a coinflip — you only have Q and one passive shot, and Yone trades evenly this early, so just last-hit at Q range and don't walk into his W cleave. From 2 you take over: your second passive shot and Q poke out-range his melee Q dash, and once E lands at 3 you can swing-poke and escape anything he commits. The trap is his Q3 — landing two Qs empowers his third into a dash-knockup; bait it out or stand so it whiffs, because without it he can't pin you for a W follow-up.
edits.after: Level 1 is a coinflip — you only have Q and one passive shot, and Yone trades evenly this early, so last-hit at Q range and stay out of Spirit Cleave (W), a 700-range cone that also SHIELDS him. From 2 you take over: your second passive shot and Q out-range Mortal Steel's 450, and once E lands at 3 you swing-poke and escape anything he commits. The trap is Gathering Storm — two Mortal Steel hits empower the next into a dash-knockup, so bait it or stand where it whiffs.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your strongest pure-laning window — your lower E cooldown and Q chip let you stack the passive third-hit shield on him every trade while he can't answer the range. The key read is his E (spirit-rewind): it banks his position and refunds damage taken, so if he dashes in he can simply undo the trade. Bait that E first, then commit. At 6 your R is the finisher on a Yone you've already poked low — the missing-HP scaling means even his E-back can't save him if you channel as he over-commits his Q3 into R.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your strongest pure-laning window — your low E cooldown and Q chip stack the passive third-hit shield every trade while he can't answer the range. The key read is Soul Unbound (E): his spirit leaves the body, and when it ends he snaps back to where that body stood, repeating part of the damage he dealt. It is an escape route, not a heal — strip it by baiting the 22s, then commit. At 6 Comeuppance finishes a Yone you have poked low; channel it as he over-commits the dash into Fate Sealed.

edits.before: You must have a lead banked by your first-item spike, because this flips hard. At 2+ crit items Yone becomes a mobile, durable carry — his Q dash and E let him close the gap your kiting depended on, his Q3 knockup and R catch you out of Heroic Swing, and he simply out-stats your lethality once he's beefy. You stay squishy and your passive shield only helps if trades go your way, so don't duel a fed Yone late. Convert your early kills into towers and use W's roam tools to swing the map before his scaling makes the lane unwinnable.
edits.after: You must have a lead banked by your first-item spike, because this flips hard. notes: Two real corrections behind the naming fix the packet flagged. Soul Unbound was described four times as undoing damage or refunding HP — Riot's text says the spirit returns to the BODY'S position and repeats a portion of the damage HE dealt. It is a position rewind and an escape, not sustain, and an Akshan who thinks it heals will never commit. Fate Sealed is a pull, not a pin: he blinks behind the last champion in the line and drags everyone hit toward him. And Spirit Cleave was written off as a melee cleave when it is a 700-range cone that shields him, which is the ability most likely to eat your burst window. All five ability names are now on the page, plus Soul Unbound's 22s rank-1 cooldown as the commit cue and the Gathering Storm two-stack framing in place of the opaque 'Q3'.
